headline: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra controls robot arms with 2.4x higher success, 2.3x lower cost
summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra demonstrated remarkable efficiency in robotic tasks, achieving a 95% success rate on a block-in-bowl task, significantly outperforming Fable 5.1 and Fable 5 while being faster and cheaper.
details: OpenAI's new GPT-6 Astra model has been tested controlling YAM robot arms, showing significant advancements in task completion. In a "pick up red block and place in bowl" task, Astra achieved a 95% success rate.

This compares dramatically to Fable 5.1's 40% and Fable 5's 5% completion rates on the same task. Astra also completed the bowl task in an average of 2.5 minutes per trial, much faster than Fable 5.1's 6.8 minutes.
The estimated cost per run for Astra on the bowl task was $0.94, making it 2.3 times cheaper than Fable 5.1's $2.12. This highlights a notable improvement in both efficiency and cost-effectiveness.

However, on a more complex "puzzle piece into groove" task, Astra's performance was on par with Fable 5.1, both completing it 2 out of 20 times. Astra still offered a cost advantage, estimated at $1.36 per run compared to Fable 5.1's $2.18.

All trials were scored by human graders based on the highest stage reached, ensuring even failed runs provided valuable data on progress. The methodology remained consistent with previous Fable model comparisons.

headline_marked: [[ISAR Aerospace's Spectrum rocket reaches orbit]], first from Western European soil
headline: ISAR Aerospace's Spectrum rocket reaches orbit, first from Western European soil
summary: German company Isar Aerospace successfully launched its Spectrum rocket from Norway, marking the first orbital launch from Western Europe and deploying multiple payloads.
details: German company Isar Aerospace has made history with its Spectrum rocket, successfully reaching orbit from the Andøya Space Center in northern Norway. This marks the first time a rocket has achieved orbit from Western European soil, a significant milestone for the continent's space industry. The launch occurred on September 5th at 4:12 p.m. EDT.

The two-stage, 95-foot-tall Spectrum rocket settled into an elliptical path around Earth just over seven minutes after liftoff. Nikolaos Perakis, Spectrum chief engineer, expressed immense pride, stating, "This is right now making history — making history for Spectrum, making history for Isar, making history for Europe."

This successful mission, dubbed 'Onward and Upward,' was Spectrum's second orbital attempt. Its debut flight in March 2025, 'Going Full Spectrum,' experienced an anomaly and crashed shortly after launch due to an unintended vent valve opening and loss of attitude control.

Isar Aerospace conducted a comprehensive investigation, learning from the failure and implementing fixes. The second flight faced multiple delays, including issues with a pressurization valve, bad weather, an intruding boat, a composite overwrapped pressure vessel leak, and off-nominal fluid system behavior.

Despite the setbacks, the company persevered, bringing the rocket back to the pad for its successful launch. Unlike its debut, this flight carried viable payloads: five cubesats and one non-deployable scientific experiment.

The mission achieved full success after the upper stage performed a circularization burn to adjust its elliptical orbit and successfully deployed all payloads. The initial orbit ranged from 112 miles (180 km) to 311 miles (500 km) from Earth.

Isar Aerospace envisions Spectrum becoming a workhorse for small to medium-size satellites, capable of hauling up to 2,200 pounds (1,000 kilograms) to low Earth orbit. Its Munich facility can produce over 30 rockets annually, supporting this ambitious vision.

While Spectrum is the first from Western Europe, other parts of the continent, specifically the Russian Plesetsk Cosmodrome, have hosted orbital launches for about six decades. This achievement firmly places Western Europe on the orbital launch map.
